analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. These units change documentation, not executable controls; no independently supported security regression was identified. Selected-model recovery adds scheduled loads and selective eviction (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, head patch lines 371–408), relevant to A-018, TB-007, T-029 and TB-012/T-059. The documented design preserves memory admission, selected models, pins, leases and in-flight work, with backoff and victim rechecks. docs/architecture/addon-hold.md:65–68 extends hold deferral and cancellation to recovery and coordinator preloads without changing the stated App Attest lifecycle. No changes to key custody, encryption, cache scope or persistence controls are evidenced; T-041's reviewed cache protections are not altered by these documents.
Integration must verify ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift against model loading/admission and enterAddonHold: cancellation must settle native ownership, victim checks must survive asynchronous races, and held or draining states must prevent publication and admission. changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md:7 also documents disconnected drain completion and bounded shutdown unloads; examine ProviderLoop+PlannedDisconnect.swift and shutdown retirement to ensure the grace period does not bypass outstanding work or connection authorization invalidation (T-010, T-053). Line 8 introduces a pending-owner-review policy that drains a continuously busy adopted model after ten minutes; reconcile its admission suppression and coordinator routing behavior with recovery and A-018. Implementation evidence is absent from this batch, so these material contracts remain unverified rather than findings. Existing surrounding failure modes were not treated as new issues.
